messages:
maria_support: Customer "ACME App" reporting intermittent 429s from /v1/rerank since ~09:12 PST. They say overall QPS is low (~5 req/s) but concurrent batch sizes are high.
jonah_sre: Can you paste a sample request + headers (no PII)? 429 body and headers would be helpful (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-*)
maria_support: Here’s redacted curl they ran: `curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank -d '{"query":"find best matches","candidates":["... 200 items ..."],"top_k":5}'` Response: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"rate limit exceeded"}` Headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 120`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `Retry-After: 10`
alex_ml: 120 what? tokens? requests? Which limit is that showing? Rerank is sensitive to candidate count since we internally expand scoring ops for each candidate. If they send 200 candidates that's 200 scoring ops per request.
emily_cs: Customer insists they only do 5 req/s. Their telemetry: 5 concurrent requests each with 200 candidates -> 1000 scoring ops/s.
jonah_sre: That makes sense — our per-customer request-rate quota is based on scoring ops not raw req/s. We should confirm with logs: can you grab request_id(s) from their 429 responses?
maria_support: They provided two examples: req id `r-0a1b2c3d` at 09:14:12 and `r-0a1b2c4e` at 09:14:15.
jonah_sre: Thanks. I've pulled logs: both show quota throttle: `quota_exceeded: scoring_ops` and backlog on the rerank pool. They hit burst window.
alex_ml: Also check payload shape — large candidate strings increase tokenization cost. If candidates are long we count more tokens. Do we have token estimates?
maria_support: Customer says candidates are short ids (~8 chars) but they batch a lot of them.
emily_cs: Customer asks for mitigation: they want to avoid 429s without changing product behavior. Any immediate suggestions?
jonah_sre: Short term: reduce concurrency (parallel requests) or reduce candidates per request. Add exponential backoff honoring Retry-After. We can also suggest using our batch rerank helper in SDK which chunks automatically.
alex_ml: Medium term: we can offer to raise their scoring_ops quota for Dedicated/enterprise or suggest they use a lower-cost approximate reranker (embedding-based prefilter) before calling rerank to reduce candidates.
maria_support: Sent that advice to customer. They requested a temporary quota bump while they refactor.
jonah_sre: I'll file a quota escalation. @quota-bot can you create a ticket to increase scoring_ops limit for org `acme-app` to 5000/s for next 72h and mark P1? Include request ids.
quota-bot: Ticket created: Q-98765. Requested increase to 5000 scoring_ops/s for acme-app for 72h. Owner: quota-ops.
emily_cs: Customer accepted temporary bump, will implement client-side chunking and backoff. Also asked for a short doc explaining how scoring_ops are calculated.
\alex_ml: I'll draft a short note: scoring_ops ~= number_of_candidates * model_cost_factor (and tokenization for long candidates). Recommend keep candidates <= 50 per request for heavy models.
j onah_sre: Follow-ups: (1) confirm SDK chunking behavior for rerank; (2) add a telemetry dashboard for scoring_ops per-org; (3) consider returning clearer header naming for rerank (X-RW-ScoringOps-Limit).
maria_support: Noted. Customer will test changes later today and report. Closing loop once no 429s for 24h. :thumbsup:
